subsystems.name: Chassis
subsystems.role: defines the robot's shape and holds the other components together.

subsystems.name: Targeting and sensing
subsystems.role: recognise specific cells, viruses or DNA sequences and trigger action only there.

subsystems.name: Actuator
subsystems.role: performs a mechanical task such as opening a lid, walking along a track or applying force.

subsystems.name: Payload
subsystems.role: carries the therapeutic agent to be delivered or the tool for repair.

subsystems.name: Control and power
subsystems.role: keeps the robot inactive until it reaches the target and supplies energy for movement.

buildSteps.title: Design the structure
buildSteps.detail: Software designs DNA sequences that will fold into a planned shape with binding sites for sensors, actuators and payload.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise DNA strands
buildSteps.detail: Short oligonucleotides are made by solid-phase chemical synthesis and mixed in the right ratios.

buildSteps.title: Self-assemble
buildSteps.detail: The mixture is heated and slowly cooled so the strands anneal into the intended DNA origami or cage.

buildSteps.title: Add functional modules
buildSteps.detail: Aptamers, logic gates and molecular motors are attached at defined positions.

buildSteps.title: Load the payload
buildSteps.detail: Therapeutic molecules are encapsulated inside the structure or conjugated to it.

buildSteps.title: Test in vitro
buildSteps.detail: The robot is tested in test tubes for correct folding, target binding and triggered release.

buildSteps.title: Test in cells and animals
buildSteps.detail: Cell cultures and animal models are used to check targeting, safety, immune response and effectiveness.

buildSteps.title: Clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: If preclinical tests succeed, the therapy enters human trials for specific diseases.

prerequisites.tech: DNA origami and structural DNA nanotechnology
prerequisites.why: provides the building blocks for precise molecular shapes and attachment points.
DNA walkers and other motors have been demonstrated, but not yet robust inside living bodies.
some targeted therapies exist, but molecular robots need better cell-specific addressing.
the body's immune system would otherwise clear or attack the robots before they act.
there is no proven way to steer or monitor individual molecular robots deep inside the body.

pathway.milestone: in vitro demonstrations of DNA robots that walk, sort cargo or open in response to a trigger
pathway.unlocks: proof that molecular machines can perform useful tasks.

pathway.milestone: robots that target specific cells in culture and release a payload
pathway.unlocks: validation of targeting and control in living systems.

pathway.milestone: safe and effective treatment in animal disease models
approved therapies for targeted diseases such as cancer
pathway.unlocks: routine molecular surgery, possibly including DNA repair.
